Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph 14 NOV 2019 OPINION NO. S. HON. JOSEPH G. UAYAN Mayor Sagay, Camiguin Dear Mayor Uayan: This has reference to your letter requesting our legal opinion on what to do with the claim for back wages of Carmelita S. Bonachita-Ricablanca, a former member of the Sangguniang Barangay of Barangay Poblacion, Sagay, Camiguin and now an incumbent member of the Sangguniang Bayan of Sagay, and its computation. Per records, it appears that in an Amended Decision dated 29 June 2018, the Court of Appeals (Former 21st Division), Cagayan de Oro granted respondent Bonachita-RicabIanca's Motion for Reconsideration to the CA Decision dated 30 June 2017 and accordingly, reversed the Ombudsman Decision dated 13 October 2015 finding her liable for grave misconduct and conduct prejudicial to the best interest of the service and meting upon her the penalty of dismissal from the service. Per your representation, your good office has already issued on 18 February 2019 an assumption to office order to respondent Bonachita-RicabIanca. Hence, your request for legal opinion. In reply thereto, we are of the view that respondent Bonachita-Ricablanca is not entitled to backwages. In a letter dated 21 April 20171, the Office of the Ombudsman, through Assistant Ombudsman Asryman Rafanan, laid down the conditions necessary for the grant of back salaries in administrative disciplinary cases, thus: As held by the Court in Civil Service Commission v. Cruz, there are two conditions necessary for the grant of back salaries in administrative disciplinary cases, namely: a the e Io und nt ch es; and b) his suspension must be unjustified. Hence, back salaries shall be paid only if the government official or employee is completely exonerated of the charge against him and his suspension or dismissal is found and declared to be unjustified. (Emphasis Supplied) Upon perusal of the reasons cited by the CA in its Amended Decision, we learned the following: I Printed copy attached.

1. The CA applied the recent case of Almario-Templenuevo vs. Office of the Ombudsman3, wherein the Supreme Court, on appeal, reversed the Court of Appeals and ruled that the condonation doctrine Wi" apply. despite its abandonment in the case of Carpio Morales vs. Court of Appeals and even if it involved a public officer who was elected to a different position provided that it is shown that the body politic electing the person to another office is the same as held in the case of Giron v. Ochoa; 2. The CA found the condonation doctrine applicable in the case of respondent Bonachit@-Ricablanqa following the Supreme Court's ruling in the Almario-Templonuevo vs. Ombudsman case. When one is condoned like herein respondent Bonachita-Ricablanca, it does not mean that she was also found "innocent of the charges". These two terms are different from each other. The latter is one of the two (2) conditions in order for one to become entitled to back salaries. The term "innocent of the charges" requires that respondent must not be found guilty (even the slightest wrongdoing) of the offense charged. "Condonation" or the Condonation Doctrine, on the other hand, implies that respondent should have been found guilty by the court of the offense charged but due to his re-election to office, there is an assumption that the electorate disregarded or forgave his fault or misconduct. It arises from the principle that it iS not for the court, by reason of such fault or misconduct, to practically overrule the will of the people. It is apparent in the discussion of the Court of Appeals in its Amended Decision that respondent Bonachita-RicabIanca should have been found guilty of the offense charge were it not for the timely issuance by the Supreme Court of its ruling in the Almario-Templenuevo applying the condonation doctrine. As such, respondent Bonachita-RicabIanca cannot be said that he is "innocent of the charges". We hope to have addressed your concerns accordingly. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: MARIVEL C. CENDONCILLO, CESO 111 Undersec tary for Local Governmen Ls/LRALLD/17 Copy furnished: DIR. ARNEL M.
